marta.sales: Hi team — enterprise wants a 10-day Dedicated POC (Azure). Their security team insists on a single IPv4 for outbound allowlisting (one /32). They also want per-environment API tokens (dev/stage/poc) and a short SOW + lead time. Any blockers?
nile.eng: We can create per-project scoped API tokens and TTL them for the POC window. For billing: POC is pro-rated Dedicated reservation + one-time provisioning fee; finance can confirm final numbers.
sam.network: For a single /32 on Azure we should reserve a Public IP and attach it to our NAT Gateway or use a Public IP Prefix with one address. Important: to guarantee the same IP across the POC window we must constrain the Dedicated cluster to a single egress gateway and avoid cross-AZ scaling/failover. Call that out in the SOW.
marta.sales: If they want HA but still a single IP, is that possible?
sam.network: HA with a strict single IP is a tradeoff. We can do active/passive with floating IP, but that increases complexity and lead time. For short POCs easiest: single AZ + pinned NAT IP.
quinn.solutions: SOW snippet for copy/paste: "Provision temporary Dedicated cluster (N GPUs) constrained to a single egress gateway to guarantee static outbound IP (single /32); generate time-limited API tokens scoped to POC environments; run smoke tests; provide monitoring access. Customer to add provided IP and hostname to perimeter allowlist."
marta.sales: They asked whether TLS terminates at our edge or on their side for peered setups.
nile.eng: With public egress TLS terminates at our edge. If they choose private endpoint/VNet peering we can preserve end-to-end TLS and optionally support mTLS — that's extra work and will extend lead time.
sam.network: Two deployment options to propose:
1) Fast path: static public NAT IP (/32) + timeboxed tokens. Lead time ~48-72h.
2) Secure path: Azure private endpoint / VNet peering (no public IP). Lead time ~5-10 business days depending on their network approvals.
marta.sales: Any sample allowlist rules and a quick curl I can send them?
sam.network: Yes — recommend allowing both IP and hostname in case their proxy validates SNI:
ALLOW TCP 443 to 203.0.113.210/32
ALLOW HOST: dedicated.az.redwood.example.com
And the curl: 
```
curl -v --resolve "dedicated.az.redwood.example.com:443:203.0.113.210" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://dedicated.az.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"ping"}'
```
quinn.solutions: Also call out DNS: if they allow hostnames, their firewall must honor DNS TTLs. For strict single-IP allowlist prefer the /32 route. Recommend short-lived tokens + IP allowlist for best security.
marta.sales: Lead time I can promise in the email?
nile.eng: Estimate: SOW signed and billing cleared day 0. If we have spare IP in our pool, reserve same day; otherwise we request IP allocation (1 business day). Cluster + NAT attach (1 business day). Keys + smoke tests (same day). So ~2-3 business days for fast path. Private peering add 3-7+ days.
sre-bot: Created ticket SRE-8123 to reserve IP 203.0.113.210 and schedule Dedicated cluster creation. Assigned to sam.network. ETA 72h. :white_check_mark:
marta.sales: Perfect — I'll send both options and the SOW snippet. I'll ask which they prefer and request the signed SOW. Will update once they choose.
